launch.session_origin: host; correlation only, not a security credential or reset detector

vm.disabled_endpoints: QMP/GDB omitted (disabled by default); monitor explicitly none; no networking or shares
vm.firmware_format: raw pflash: 3653632-byte code + 540672-byte fresh vars = 4 MiB
vm.local_apic: CPU APIC capability retained; guest register discovery pending

limitations: TCG one-vCPU 2GiB capacity profile; no desktop memory/CPU/input acceptance
mandatory timing/outcome instrumentation remains in both profiles; sampled dispatch/wake quantiles have complete maxima but not every tail sample
HPET elapsed intervals and host process elapsed are separate; no CPU/RSS claim
synthetic ephemeral routes, manual trusted bootstrap, experimental supervision IDs; no reload/durability/security certification; M3 exit remains open

criterion_review.continuous_faults: pass: ten distinct continuous guests, 100 waves each, 200 worker lifecycles and 100 route cycles per guest; expected process-local faults and healthy control checksums
criterion_review.reclamation: pass: every staged/death/settled resource row independently reconciled; all 100 settled baselines identical within each guest and final frame/object/wait inventories zero
criterion_review.physical_accounting: pass: eligible/free/resident partition, physical backing counted once, private/shared/queued holds, owner/orphan attribution, fixed image/table/sample capacity and launch refusal
criterion_review.timing: pass: 100000 measured IPC samples plus 10000 warmups, fixed-stride dispatch/wake samples with complete maxima, HPET expiry/timer lateness, 64 idle halts per guest and paired observer cost
criterion_review.regressions: pass: fresh P3-12 complete runtime gate, 95 host tests, separate public supervision and 14 separate metadata flavors; fixed deadlines/quotas and failed development provenance retained

unsafe_review.boundary: registered user_fixture hooks; checked dispatcher and common return validation retained; public operations cannot select return IP/selectors/privileged flags
unsafe_review.copy_and_reap: real nested timer interrupt while map/transfer copy pin is live requests deferred death; return observer asserts successful commit and zero pins before trusted reap; no registry borrow or kernel continuation crosses task switch
unsafe_review.measurement: single CPU, IF-clear bounded static observer state; fixed-capacity buffers reject overflow; mandatory queue peaks remain observed on inline traffic and ownership scans occur on transfer/ownership changes; snapshots and trace samples are read-only
unsafe_review.public_fixture: only frozen SDK and packaged pure policy/routes code in isolated locked/offline build; little-endian test records and kernel-authenticated receive identities; explicit handles closed or reaped; all actual user ELFs reviewed for admitted x87/SSE2 baseline
unsafe_review.scope: trusted synthetic bootstrap and experimental supervision IDs are explicit test facilities; not a general SDK extension, thread model, hostile-code certification, guest UI or reload result

sdk.kernel: registered user_fixture observer and existing checked dispatcher/return-state validation; public operations cannot select return IP/selectors/privileged flags; one CPU and original deadlines/quotas
sdk.register_boundary: raw pointer-bearing wrapper remains unsafe; R8/R9 zero, RAX/RDX/RCX/R11 and memory clobbers; explicit little-endian records rather than Rust layout; actual ELF and ISO payload identities checked
sdk.allocator: single owning thread with no callback/signal reentry; private RW 64 KiB object, source handle closed after map; 64-byte cells/32 slots/alignment <=4096; zero before return, matching deallocation, live-allocation shutdown denied; default allocate-copy-free realloc preserves old allocation on failure
sdk.fp_and_dependencies: kernel FP state access limited to eager fxsave64/fxrstor64 helpers and the audited MXCSR control reader or guarded entry snapshot; no kernel FP arithmetic; admitted user SSE2 instruction whitelist and no AVX/XSAVE/CPU dispatch or unresolved imports; selected model/segmentation/libm only execute in runtime guest
sdk.authority: numeric identities and startup/checkpoint bytes confer no authority; receive outputs usable only after success; transferred handles explicitly closed on protocol rejection; existing current-session/policy/revision/deadline and writer-fence rules retained
sdk.limits: trusted synthetic bootstrap; one thread/process, masked SSE exceptions, no shared-process threads/TLS/SMP, no full text/font/raster/display guest, durable policy, state migration, safe old-code retirement or general SDK release

stress.boundary: registered user_fixture hooks; checked dispatcher and common return validation retained; public operations cannot select return IP/selectors/privileged flags
stress.copy_and_reap: real nested timer interrupt while map/transfer copy pin is live requests deferred death; return observer asserts successful commit and zero pins before trusted reap; no registry borrow or kernel continuation crosses task switch
stress.measurement: single CPU, IF-clear bounded static observer state; fixed-capacity buffers reject overflow; mandatory queue peaks remain observed on inline traffic and ownership scans occur on transfer/ownership changes; snapshots and trace samples are read-only
stress.public_fixture: only frozen SDK and packaged pure policy/routes code in isolated locked/offline build; little-endian test records and kernel-authenticated receive identities; explicit handles closed or reaped; all actual user ELFs reviewed for admitted x87/SSE2 baseline
stress.scope: trusted synthetic bootstrap and experimental supervision IDs are explicit test facilities; not a general SDK extension, thread model, hostile-code certification, guest UI or reload result

unsafe_review.host: private kill-on-close Windows jobs contain command descendants; real replay uses exact ISO, fresh locked vars, no host shares/network/disks; all spawned QEMU processes waited

limits: one vCPU, one thread/process, eager x87/SSE2 with masked SSE exceptions
ephemeral synthetic identities/policy/routes; surviving direct mappings end at owner teardown
only exact SDK contract subset frozen; supervision/later desktop families experimental
no guest UI/input/render/reload, state migration, safe old-code retirement, durability or real accounts
